label: TP
reason: Both alerts are alert-TP. Alert 1 (java/xss): User-controlled data flows through param→bar→fileTarget→fileTarget.toString()→encodeForHTML() to the HTML response sink. While encoding is present, per balanced encoding rule, attacker-controlled data reaching the sink warrants alert-TP rather than automatic dismissal. Alert 2 (java/path-injection): User-controlled param flows directly to fileTarget used in new File(bar) with no validation or restriction, enabling path traversal. This is a confirmed vulnerability.

evidence.note: User input extracted from request.getParameterMap() at L43-L50, passed to doSomething() at L53, assigned to bar at L69, used to create fileTarget at L60
XSS sink: encodeForHTML(fileTarget.toString()) outputs user-controlled file path to HTML response
Path injection sink: fileTarget variable used directly in new File() constructor with no validation
